card.title: How To Fix iPhone 7 That Has No Backlight or Dark Spot On Screen

source.title: How To Fix iPhone 7 That Has No Backlight or Dark Spot On Screen

claims.statement: iPhone 7 no backlight is usually a blown backlight filter: FL3901, FL3902, FL3903 on iPhone 7; FL3901, FL3902, FL3903, FL4601, FL4602 on 7 Plus.
Find a backlight pin at the LCD connector reading OL (PP_LCM_BL_CAT1/CAT2/ANODE_CONN, plus BL34 lines on 7 Plus); a good filter has continuity and equal readings on both sides.
Never replace a filter with a jumper wire; use the same value part.

procedure: Confirm board fault (known-good screen, charge current, flashlight).
Diode-check LCD connector backlight pins against boardview (±5–10%).
Test filters for continuity; replace blown ones with the correct value.
Re-check the pin reading and test.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Jumpering a filter removes surge protection and can permanently damage the phone.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
